- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.5) and forecast is trending down, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5) and forecast is trending up, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to account for bearish sentiment.  
- If forecast shows a sharp upward spike followed by a steep decline, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast is flat or slowly rising but true outcome shows strong mean reversion downward, shift forecast downward by 2–5% in the next 5–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if history shows volatility >10% over last 18 days, apply a 3–5% downward bias to avoid overconfidence in smooth trends.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 entries, assume low conviction and apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to forecast to reflect uncertainty.
